The architecture already has a vendor-neutral core under `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations`, with provider namespaces supplying vendor-specific behavior. **Instead is the only registered adapter today.** `gruntworx` exists in the provider enum, but has no registry entry; Juno still has a legacy integration outside these ports.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

| Area | Core responsibility |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connections | Start/complete authorization; report, disconnect, renew, verify and revoke grants. |
| Export | Authorize access, validate files against capabilities, find/create the tax-preparation envelope, create send records, then delegate execution. |
| Recovery and reconciliation | Resume interrupted sends after reconnect; periodically ask adapters to reconcile processing statuses. |
| Tax-preparation lifecycle | Prefill export forms, delete preparations, and merge records when contacts merge. |
| Firm lifecycle | Disconnect grants across providers and remove both shared and vendor-specific records. |
| Shared infrastructure | OAuth/token lifecycle, HTTP/error handling, signed-target byte transfer, upload/processing states and status broadcasts. |

The core calls `adapter::ExportAsync` with shared records; it does not prescribe the vendor’s upload sequence. Instead implements its own workflow: resolve/create an entity, then start upload → transfer bytes → finalize upload for each file.

Sources: [core export](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53), [Instead workflow](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/export_async_workflow.rb:23).

**Registration and adapter contract**

Registration is explicit, through `Registry::ADAPTERS`:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = { instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead }.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = { instead: :tax_automations_instead }.freeze
```

Normal requests resolve the adapter through the firm’s settings. Authorization names the requested provider explicitly, so switching vendors can start while the old provider remains selected. Historical sends retain their own provider; cleanup and background work can address adapters independently of the current selection.

The interface is a namespace convention enforced by production dispatch sites:

| Required member in the adapter namespace | Contract used by the core |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | ActiveRecord model with firm lookup, usable/connected scopes, grant lifecycle, token storage and `.capabilities`. |
| `Client` | Constructed with a connection; supports shared OAuth renewal/revocation and signed-target upload where used. Instead subclasses `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)`; returns the connection. |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)` |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids: ...})` |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)` |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` |

These services follow the shared service-result convention. The reconciliation member is required by a background sweep, even though it is not part of the interactive export path.

Connections use `HasOauthConnection`: encrypted tokens, their expiries, creator identity, timestamps, and `disconnected / connected / expired / revoked` states. An `expired` connection remains usable because renewal may restore it.

Sources: [registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3), [connection concern](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:24), [background reconciliation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:35).

**Capability passport**

The passport is a typed, class-level description of the vendor, available without a connection row:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

An adapter’s connection implements private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`; `HasCapabilities` expands and validates them.

Key properties:

- Formats and size limits belong to each return type.
- Supported return types are derived from the terms.
- Unknown return types have no terms and are rejected.
- Duplicate return-type declarations and malformed values raise errors when `.capabilities` is called.
- Tax years must be integers from 2000 through the current year plus one.

Instead declares the same format/size terms for its mapped forms and supports the current tax year plus the previous two. Formats and limits come from settings.

The shared export validator applies this passport before dispatch. The API translates it into `tax_years` and enriched `return_types`, each containing `value`, `name`, personal/business `type`, `file_types`, and `file_size_limit`.

Sources: [passport definition](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:20), [validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:38), [API representation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:9).

**Data model**

| Entity | Purpose and identity |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One row per firm; selected provider and external vendor-account binding. Provider enum: `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| Shared `TaxPreparation` | Return envelope: firm, client, optional contact, year, return type, EIN and business name. Core uniqueness is firm + client + contact + year. |
| Shared `Document` | A source document sent under an envelope, provider and return type. Unique across those identifiers plus firm. Stores upload state, processing state, failure reason and upload timestamp. |
| Instead `Connection` | One grant per firm, with a polymorphic staff creator, encrypted OAuth credentials and vendor-specific PKCE ceremony fields. |
| Instead `Entity` | Vendor taxpayer identity: external UUID, entity type, client/contact linkage, source and synchronization/archive information. External UUID is unique within a firm. |
| Instead `Document` | One-to-one extension of a shared send record; holds the Instead entity, vendor file UUID and path. |

The shared send record owns two independent state machines:

- Upload: `waiting → uploading → uploaded`, with failure/reset paths.
- Processing: `sent → processing → processed`, with error, exceeded, archive and resend paths.

Its provider and return type are snapshots, so changing firm settings or the envelope does not rewrite what an earlier send represented.

There is still a migration boundary: the shared `TaxPreparation` model physically uses `juno_tax_preparations` and retains Juno-specific associations alongside the new core fields. GruntWorx therefore has an architectural insertion point, but adding its enum value alone does not implement the adapter contract.

Sources: [firm settings](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firm_settings.rb:6), [shared envelope](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:3), [shared send record](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3), [Instead entity](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/entity.rb:3), [Instead document extension](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/document.rb:3).
